subject: SOC 2 evidence + bespoke deletion window for Halcyon Health
messages:
From: Samantha Price <samantha.price@halcyonhealth.com>
To: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: Mike Tran <mike.tran@halcyonhealth.com>
Date: 2026-06-28T09:12:00Z
Subject: SOC 2 evidence + retention questions for Halcyon Health

Neha —

Thanks for the fast intro last week. As part of our procurement review I need to confirm Redwood's data lifecycle controls for two narrow scopes: (1) per-tenant log retention (we have a mixed multitenant environment where some customers are regulated) and (2) customer-triggered deletion/forensic hold behavior. Halcyon is evaluating a production rollout and the security team needs concrete evidence for our SOC 2 file and the CAIQ.

High-level asks:
- Can you provide the specific SOC 2 control excerpts or a redacted SOC 2 report section that documents log retention and deletion controls?
- For logs: can retention be set per-tenant to 365 days for PHI-related processing and 90 days for standard debug traces?
- For deletion: what is the proof-of-delete process (artifact), and can you support an extended legal hold that prevents deletion when we request it?
- Any CAIQ/ SIG/ CAIC mappings you can share that call out these behaviors would be very helpful.

We would like to see a sample proof-of-delete artifact and the timeline for turnaround (we're targeting contract signature by end of Q3). If possible, please include any runbook entries or process notes describing exceptional retention requests.

Thanks — Samantha
Security Program Manager
Halcyon Health

Attachment: halcyon_initial_ask.pdf (stub)
From: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, jordan.blake@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-06-28T11:04:00Z
Subject: Re: SOC 2 evidence + retention questions for Halcyon Health

Samantha —

Appreciate the details and the target dates. Looping in Ben (security & compliance) and Jordan (legal/contracts) to scope the exact artifacts and confirm timelines. Initial responses inline below; Ben and Jordan will follow up with the evidence pack and clarifying questions.

Inline:
- SOC 2 excerpts: we can provide a redacted SOC 2 report summary that highlights CC6/CC7 controls related to system operations and data lifecycle.
- Per-tenant retention: our platform supports tenant-scoped TTL on telemetry and debug logs; we can propose policies to set 90d/365d buckets and document the configuration.
- Proof-of-delete: we maintain deletion audit-events and a signed proof-of-delete artifact (hash + timestamp + operator id) that we can share as a sample.
- Legal hold: we support suspension of automatic deletion and a documented hold workflow; needs a signed request and a brief SLA to define retention during hold.

Action items (initial):
1) Ben to prepare evidence list and earliest delivery date.
2) Jordan to flag any contract language required for per-tenant TTL and holds.
3) I will schedule a 1-hour workshop next week to walk Halcyon through artifacts.

Proposed timeline: evidence pack (initial) by 2026-06-30 EOD, full artifact set by 2026-07-07. Are those workable?

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
T: +1 415 555 0198

Samantha / Neha —

Thanks — I pulled the list together and sketched what we can provide immediately. Short version up front: yes, we can support per-tenant retention buckets and legal holds; we can deliver a redacted SOC 2 excerpt, a CAIQ mapping, and a sample proof-of-delete within the timelines Neha suggested.

Evidence we'll attach in the initial pack:
- redwood_SOC2_summary_2025.pdf (redacted sections covering change management and data lifecycle controls)
- redwood_CAIC_filled_halcyon.xlsx (CAIQ/ SIG mapping with callouts on per-tenant TTL and hold workflow)
- sample_proof_of_delete_HALCYON.txt (signed proof-of-delete example with hash and audit-event links)
- runbook_snippet_retention_override.md (short stub describing exceptions workflow)

Technical notes:
- Retention model: tenant metadata includes a retention_profile field. The serving runtime enforces TTL at ingestion and a background erasure job runs daily; per-tenant overrides are supported via the admin console and API.
- Proof-of-delete: generated as a signed manifest with SHA256 for the deleted blobs, timestamp (UTC), operator-id, and a link to the audit-event in the console. We retain the audit-event and manifest for 180 days by default (longer by request).
- Legal hold: hold requests flip the tenant retention_profile to 'hold' and suspend erasure jobs for the tenant; holds are recorded in the audit log and require a signed ticket. Holds can be timeboxed or indefinite.

Clarifying questions for Halcyon (so we can scope the deliverables):
1) For the 365-day PHI retention bucket, do you need immutable snapshots (WORM-style) or is administrative hold + proof-of-delete on un-hold sufficient?
2) For legal hold, what is your expected SLA for notification to Redwood before removal (e.g., 30 days)?
3) Any specific CAIQ control IDs you want us to highlight beyond the usual e.g., IA/DR/Logging?

Delivery: I'll put the initial evidence pack into a secured Drive link and share by 2026-06-30 18:00 PT. If you need anything redacted differently for legal review, tell us what fields to remove and Jordan will confirm.

Ben Carter
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Attachments referenced: redwood_SOC2_summary_2025.pdf (stub), redwood_CAIC_filled_halcyon.xlsx (stub), sample_proof_of_delete_HALCYON.txt (stub)

Ben / Neha —

Thanks for the quick turn. A few clarifications from our security/legal side so you can tailor the pack:
- For EMR-related logs (tracebacks, request/response metadata that may contain PHI) we must retain 365 days and need a documented tamper-evidence mechanism. An administrative hold alone is acceptable if we can get an immutable proof (signed manifest) and audit trail proving the data was not mutated while on hold.
- For standard application debug traces 90 days is fine.
- For legal hold: our counsel requires that Redwood be able to accept a hold request and (a) suspend deletion, (b) produce a time-bound acknowledgment, and (c) provide export capabilities for the preserved set within 72 hours.
- CAIQ: please map controls to CIS and specific SOC criteria where possible; call out retention-specific control IDs.

Redwood responses to these bullets will determine whether we push the procurement forward. If you can include a sample signed manifest and an example timeframe for exporting preserved data (we likely won't exercise it but we need assurance), that will help.

We can do a 45-minute workshop on 2026-07-01 10:00 PT if that works for your team.

Best —
Samantha
